stem: A 34-year-old with palatal wear confined to upper anterior teeth has sensitivity and reduced anterior interocclusal space. Periodontal health and posterior support are satisfactory. Prevention has reduced erosion activity. They request a conservative, repairable solution.

options.A: Localised additive composite using a Dahl approach
options.B: Full-mouth ceramic crowns at a new OVD
options.C: Elective endodontics and crowns on all six anterior teeth
options.D: Removal of all posterior contacts
options.E: Extract the anterior teeth and provide an implant bridge

rationale: This pattern supports localised additive palatal rehabilitation and planned occlusal adaptation without unnecessarily restoring posterior teeth.

alternatives.B: Overtreatment of an otherwise supported posterior dentition.
alternatives.D: Destabilises function instead of providing conservative space.
alternatives.E: Invasive and biologically disproportionate.

stem: A 61-year-old seeks definitive fixed reconstruction after repeated crown failures. Multiple 6–8 mm periodontal pockets bleed, plaque control is poor and mobility is increasing. A laboratory wax-up looks excellent. What is the most appropriate immediate next step?

options.A: Commence multi-unit crown preparations
options.B: Complete periodontal diagnosis, disease control and prognosis before fixed reconstruction
options.C: Extract all mobile teeth immediately
options.D: Place definitive bridges after one hygiene visit
options.E: Cement temporary bridges as permanent restorations

rationale: Active periodontal disease must be stabilised and strategic tooth prognosis established before irreversible extensive reconstruction.

alternatives.A: Biological risk has not been controlled.
alternatives.C: Some teeth may still be maintainable after assessment.
alternatives.D: One hygiene visit does not establish disease stability.
alternatives.E: Avoids diagnosis and definitive planning.

stem: A 56-year-old has severe generalised tooth wear and shortened clinical crowns, but serial images show eruption-related adaptation and a reproducible, comfortable MIP. Why is a reduced OVD not established by these findings alone?

options.A: Short crowns automatically prove collapse
options.B: Any bruxism causes OVD collapse
options.C: Alveolar compensation can preserve vertical dimension despite tooth wear
options.D: Measured freeway space is a fixed diagnostic cut-off
options.E: A visible dentine surface excludes compensation

rationale: Tooth wear and loss of OVD are distinct; compensatory dentoalveolar changes may maintain vertical dimension.

alternatives.A: Clinical crown height alone is insufficient.
alternatives.B: Wear does not establish vertical change.
alternatives.D: Freeway space is variable and must be contextualised.
alternatives.E: Dentine exposure says nothing decisive about OVD.

stem: An extensive fixed treatment is planned at a revised occlusal relationship. Repeated jaw registrations disagree by 2 mm and the mounted contacts cannot be reproduced clinically. The laboratory requests approval to mill the final crowns.

options.A: Accept the most recent digital record
options.B: Average the three records and mill
options.C: Choose a universally recommended canine guidance
options.D: Verify the patient’s reproducible reference position and record accuracy before irreversible manufacture
options.E: Increase OVD by the discrepancy amount

rationale: A reproducible clinical relationship is required before committing an extensive reorganisation. Audit record and mounting error.

alternatives.A: Digital data are not necessarily accurate.
alternatives.B: Averaging inconsistent records invents a position.
alternatives.C: Guidance choice cannot repair inaccurate jaw relation.
alternatives.E: Changes space, not the underlying registration problem.

stem: A clinician proposes a mandatory three-month removable splint evaluation for every worn dentition before any OVD increase. Which statement best reflects current consensus?

options.A: A removable splint evaluation is required for all patients
options.B: There is strong evidence evaluation phases improve all patient outcomes
options.C: OVD cannot be increased with direct composite
options.D: The only safe OVD increase is exactly 3 mm
options.E: A fixed provisional/evaluation phase may help with sequencing and expectations, but is not universally mandatory

rationale: The 2025 consensus and review found limited/inconclusive evidence for mandatory evaluation phases; interim fixed restorations can nevertheless be clinically useful.

alternatives.B: Evidence does not establish that universal effect.
alternatives.C: Direct additive approaches can be appropriate.

stem: A high-load posterior onlay is planned with adequate enamel but only 0.5 mm available clearance. The proposed lithium-disilicate system specifies more space for that indication. What is the best approach?

options.A: Reassess preparation/space and choose a material/design meeting validated specifications
options.B: Use lithium disilicate at any thickness if bonded
options.C: Use stronger acid to compensate for limited thickness
options.D: Reduce opposing sound teeth routinely
options.E: Select translucent zirconia because all zirconias share one minimum thickness

rationale: A restoration requires material- and indication-specific minimum dimensions; redesign or alternative material before committing.

alternatives.B: Bonding does not erase thickness requirements.
alternatives.E: Different zirconias and systems have differing specifications.

stem: A root-filled anterior tooth is planned as an abutment for a full-mouth bridge. Only 0.5 mm circumferential sound dentine remains above bone. Crown lengthening would severely worsen crown-root proportion and the adjacent aesthetic margin. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Assume a long post substitutes for ferrule
options.B: Reassess strategic restoratability and consider extrusion or an alternative abutment plan
options.C: Perform crown lengthening regardless of periodontal cost
options.D: Use a flexible post to strengthen the root
options.E: Place crown margins further apical without discussing tissues

rationale: Ferrule cannot be gained at any biological cost; compare extrusion, restoration redesign and extraction after prognosis assessment.

alternatives.A: Posts retain cores but do not replace coronal dentine.
alternatives.D: Post modulus is not a substitute for ferrule.
alternatives.E: Risks violation of supracrestal tissue attachment.

stem: A layered implant-supported posterior bridge chips for the third time in four years. Occlusal photographs show repeated eccentric contact on unsupported veneering porcelain and the patient reports clenching. What should be prioritised?

options.A: Remake an identical layered bridge
options.B: Treat the failure as random porcelain contamination
options.C: Address the occlusal/design problem and select a suitable retrievable restoration
options.D: Increase cusp height to guide the mandible
options.E: Place stronger cement under the existing bridge

rationale: Recurrent fracture requires examination of load, framework support and restorative design rather than automatic replacement in like-for-like form.

alternatives.E: Does not correct ceramic fracture mechanics.

stem: Six BEWE sextant scores are shown in Schematic C. A patient has no sensitivity and serial photographs show stability. What does a total BEWE score of 7 establish?

options.A: A diagnosis of bruxism
options.B: An automatic indication for full-mouth crowns
options.C: Proof of active progression
options.D: Severity of erosive wear screening requiring contextual assessment, not a treatment prescription
options.E: The exact annual micrometre loss of enamel

rationale: BEWE is an erosive-wear screening/index score; severity must be contextualised with symptoms, causes and serial data.

alternatives.A: BEWE is not a bruxism diagnosis.
alternatives.B: It does not dictate prosthesis choice.
alternatives.C: A single score does not prove progression.
alternatives.E: It is not a quantitative volumetric measurement.

stem: A full-mouth diagnostic wax-up is accepted aesthetically, but intraoral provisional closure shifts to the right. The clinical CR–MIP slide differs from the mounting record. What is the most appropriate next action?

options.A: Finish the definitive work using the wax-up
options.B: Equilibrate natural teeth immediately to the articulator
options.C: Ignore the shift because virtual models are more reliable
options.D: Create a longer zirconia bridge to prevent movement
options.E: Confirm the jaw record, provisional fit, reproducibility and functional contacts

rationale: Disagreement between models and mouth is a signal to investigate recording and provisional errors before irreversible treatment.

alternatives.C: An inaccurate record remains inaccurate digitally.
alternatives.D: Connector length does not correct occlusion.

stem: A patient is considering full-mouth crowns versus limited composite rehabilitation. Both are clinically feasible, but cost and future repairability are major priorities. What is the essential consent content?

options.A: Expected maintenance, future replacement risk, biological costs and alternatives including non-treatment
options.B: Only the initial fee and colour
options.C: Only the laboratory warranty
options.D: A statement that crowns cannot fail
options.E: A clinician decision without patient priorities

rationale: Shared decision-making includes maintenance, biological and financial risks and reasonable options.

alternatives.E: Ignores informed patient values.

stem: A patient with worn dentition has intermittent locking and painful limited mouth opening. A full-mouth reorganisation is requested to “correct the bite.” What is the best next step?

options.A: Grind to centric relation immediately
options.B: Diagnose the jaw disorder, screen red flags and use appropriate conservative management/referral before extensive reconstruction
options.C: Begin irreversible crown preparations
options.D: Increase OVD until opening normalises
options.E: Extract posterior teeth to unload the joint

rationale: Active undiagnosed orofacial pain/joint pathology warrants assessment before irreversible occlusal changes.

alternatives.D: OVD is not a proven treatment for locking.
alternatives.E: Severe and unsupported.

stem: A full-mouth digital wax-up shows excellent virtual contacts. During try-in the patient has a large unilateral premature contact. What principle best explains the discrepancy?

options.A: Virtual articulation guarantees intraoral accuracy
options.B: The crown shade changes occlusion
options.C: Scanning/registration and jaw relation may contain error; verify clinically
options.D: Occlusal contact is irrelevant to patient function
options.E: The deviation proves facial bone loss

rationale: Virtual articulation is a clinical planning aid and must be validated against an actual, repeatable mandibular relationship.

alternatives.E: Finding does not identify bone change.

stem: A proposed 14-unit fixed reconstruction involves deep subgingival crown margins on periodontally compromised teeth. The technician reports that a cleanable design is impossible at the planned contours. What is the best intervention?

options.A: Proceed because patients can floss later
options.B: Use more radiopaque cement
options.C: Place all margins even deeper for aesthetics
options.D: Redesign margins and restorative contours, reconsidering treatment suitability before preparation
options.E: Replace with the same design in zirconia

rationale: Aesthetic objectives must be balanced with periodontal health, restorative access and maintainability.

alternatives.E: Material substitution does not fix design.

stem: A patient has a stable MIP, suitable interocclusal space and an isolated defective molar crown. No other tooth requires restoration. Which occlusal approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Routine reorganised full-mouth scheme
options.B: Raise OVD on all teeth
options.C: Equilibrate the opposite arch to retruded contact position
options.D: Provide a full-mouth interim appliance before the crown
options.E: Conform to the stable existing MIP and guidance

rationale: A conformative approach is usually appropriate when the existing scheme is functional, stable and compatible with the local restoration.

stem: A patient with generalised wear needs major restorative changes but will be treated quadrant-by-quadrant. Which sequence best reduces loss of occlusal reference during rehabilitation?

options.A: Maintain reproducible reference stops with staged provisionals and verify each segment against the approved plan
options.B: Prepare all quadrants and remove every stop at the first visit
options.C: Guess contacts by patient comfort after cementation
options.D: Use unrecorded elastomeric bite material only
options.E: Rely on virtual articulation and do not check clinically

rationale: Staged rehabilitation should preserve predictable jaw relation and stable references, with provisional assessment before committing later segments.

alternatives.E: Digital tools do not eliminate chairside validation.

stem: A 49-year-old has glossy palatal erosion, recurrent sour taste at night and no posterior wear facets. They request veneers. What should the plan prioritise?

options.A: Full-mouth crowns before investigating cause
options.B: Manage possible intrinsic acid exposure and disease activity, then consider proportionate restorations
options.C: Increase OVD irrespective of symptoms
options.D: Use only an occlusal splint because all wear is bruxism
options.E: Extract palatally worn incisors

rationale: The clinical pattern suggests intrinsic acid exposure requiring medical assessment as appropriate alongside prevention and restorative planning.

alternatives.C: OVD is not the primary cause treatment.
alternatives.E: Unnecessarily invasive.

stem: A clinician proposes full-coverage zirconia crowns for all sound premolars simply because anterior veneers will be placed and the posterior occlusion is stable. What is the best evaluation?

options.A: Posterior coverage is automatically required
options.B: Restore all teeth to achieve uniform material
options.C: Prefer a minimally invasive anterior plan without unnecessary posterior preparations
options.D: Place an implant in each quadrant to share load
options.E: Remove posterior enamel to avoid potential future complications

rationale: Treatment extent must be driven by patient-specific problems; sound posterior teeth should not be sacrificed without indication.

alternatives.E: Predictive prophylactic preparation is unsupported.

stem: Five years after full-mouth rehabilitation the crowns remain cemented, but three teeth develop recurrent caries and chronic gingival inflammation. What best describes treatment success?

options.A: All crowns are successful because they remain in place
options.B: Only porcelain colour determines success
options.C: Occlusal design is irrelevant to maintenance
options.D: Survival must be distinguished from biological and patient-centred success
options.E: A radiograph is never needed once crowns are seated

rationale: Restoration survival alone does not establish biological health or patient-centred success.

alternatives.E: Investigations are justified by clinical findings.

stem: A colleague says every patient requires a “minimum 5 mm OVD increase” to reconstruct severe wear, citing a published clinical review. What is the most defensible correction?

options.A: A fixed number is valid for everyone
options.B: No increase is ever possible
options.C: Only an arbitrary articulator pin increase is relevant
options.D: The patient should choose the millimetres without diagnostic input
options.E: The change should be individually planned from anatomy, function, restorative space and goals, with provisional assessment when useful

rationale: Evidence does not establish one OVD change that is mandatory or safe for every individual.

alternatives.C: Articulator pin does not define clinical adaptation.
alternatives.D: Choice is shared but must be clinically informed.

stem: An adhesively retained restoration is planned on mostly enamel but the laboratory recommends unetched zirconia because it has higher flexural strength. What is the most appropriate reasoning?

options.A: Substrate adhesion, geometry, material processing and thickness must be considered together
options.B: Strength alone determines clinical choice
options.C: All ceramics require identical hydrofluoric conditioning
options.D: Enamel is clinically irrelevant
options.E: Monolithic zirconia always eliminates failures

rationale: Restorative selection integrates retention, bonding substrate, material-specific protocol and design rather than flexural strength alone.

alternatives.E: Overstates material guarantees.

stem: A full-mouth diagnostic wax-up is transferred to fixed provisionals. The patient develops persistent lisping and cannot achieve the closest speaking space noted before treatment. What is the best response?

options.A: Ignore speech and cement the definitive restorations
options.B: Reassess tooth position, incisal contours, OVD and provisional function, adjusting the design before final transfer
options.C: Increase only posterior crowns immediately
options.D: Extract incisors to avoid phonetic issues
options.E: Assume adaptation will always occur without review

rationale: Provisionals can reveal functional/phonetic discrepancies; the plan should be modified on measured findings.

alternatives.E: Uncertain and dismisses patient impact.

stem: In a planned full-mouth fixed reconstruction, an asymptomatic mandibular molar is missing while remaining posterior units provide stable function. The patient has limited funds and no aesthetic demand at that site. What is the most appropriate treatment-planning principle?

options.A: Every missing tooth must be replaced
options.B: Implant placement is compulsory in a comprehensive case
options.C: No replacement may be reasonable after assessing function, risk and preferences
options.D: Restore all abutments with crowns first
options.E: Avoid discussing maintenance because the site is posterior

rationale: Shortened dental-arch function and patient priorities may justify nonreplacement with review, when clinically appropriate.

alternatives.E: Maintenance discussion remains relevant.

stem: Before a complex fixed reconstruction, a specialist has recent appropriate periapicals and bitewings, stable medical history, and no clinical or radiographic reason for three-dimensional imaging. A colleague recommends routine full-arch CBCT to “complete the dataset.” Which approach is best?

options.A: Take CBCT for every full-mouth reconstruction
options.B: Use CBCT because it carries no radiation
options.C: Always obtain both full-head CBCT and a panoramic image
options.D: Justify imaging based on the specific clinical question and use existing adequate records
options.E: Avoid any radiographs regardless of dental disease

rationale: Use individually justified imaging; do not undertake 3D imaging for convenience alone when lower-dose records meet the clinical need.

alternatives.E: Can miss clinically indicated information.
